chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: What jazz really is: tempo, not music
summary: Whaley argues that jazz is tempo and swing, tells how 'jazz it up' became a word, and contrasts it with Paul Whiteman's sweet music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Music, jazz is not music. Jazz is tempo, see, years ago when Paul Whiteman was the king of syncopation, he used (sings) to play all that sweet music, see, 'Whispering' and 'I Love You,' see all that sweet music and that sophisticated swing, that's what it was. Paul Whiteman, he was the king of it. So you know, they get tired of that sweet stuff, so I used to say let's jazz this up, see, just jazz it up. Jazz was a bad word, see,

Right. So I was saying let's jazz it up and the first thing you know everybody is saying jazz, play some jazz and I tried to tell -- when I was over in Europe there, I told the guy that had the paper, I said 'why don't you ask -- put a question in your paper, what is jazz?' and you find out everybody didn't know it, didn't know what jazz was,
because jazz is not music. Jazz is tempo. Swing. It was an era of swing. And everybody was swinging and then Paul Whiteman come along with his sophisticated swing and then --
